statement: A behaviour fingerprint that counts findings by severity cannot see a finding replaced by another of the same severity. In Cejel's v26 item 8 change, the only behaviour-corpus specimen that moved swapped one info finding for another: the A3 build finding stopped firing, and the health-route branch after it in the if / else-if chain fired instead. Every fingerprint pin stayed green, because the digest excludes finding wording by design. Only the v25/v26 parity guard, which compares whole criterion fields, failed on it. Rule: for a change that can stop one finding and let a following check fire, do not read an unchanged fingerprint as no change. Measure finding identity directly (summaries per specimen, before and after), and record the count from that measurement.
